hint.label: Vocabulary

atoms.b:
Malcolm X (1925-1965)
Malcolm X was born “Malcolm Little” on May 19, 1925, in Omaha, Nebraska. He lost his father during childhood. In his teenage years, he began to engage in minor criminal acts. Then, in 1946, Malcolm was ((convicted)) of burglary and sentenced to ten years in ((prison)). While there, he began to reflect on human dignity, justice, and the importance of faith. At the same time he studied the teachings of the NOI, the religious organization Nation of Islam. The NOI advocates for African Americans to achieve economic independence and to separate from the rest of society, viewing whites as “devils”. Their views are considered controversial.

After Malcolm was ((paroled)) in 1952, he adopted the surname X to reject his “slave name” imposed by white slave masters and to symbolize his lost African heritage. Subsequently, he was chosen to be a minister and national spokesman for the NOI. Through media, he spread NOI messages across the US, while he strongly criticized the Civil Rights Movement and its non-violent approaches. He contributed to the increase in memberships in the NOI until 1963.

Moreover, he supported the separation of Black and white Americans, which stood in ((opposition)) to the integration goals advocated by ((Martin_Luther_King_Jr)). But Malcolm and Elijah Muhammad, the leader of the NOI, didn't see eye-to-eye on how to run the Nation. In 1964, Malcolm left the Nation, after a pilgrimage to Mecca softened his views on separatism. Due to growing hostility, he was assassinated by members of the NOI on February 21, 1965 in New York right before delivering a speech.
